profile.campus: Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona (CyrusOne Phoenix-metro campus, PHX1-PHX8)
profile.address: 2605 South Ellis Street, Building 8, Chandler, AZ 85286
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility materials and an aggregator listing dedicated to this specific building, PHX6 sits at 2605 South Ellis Street, Building 8, Chandler, AZ 85286, part of CyrusOne's roughly 2,000,000 sq ft, eight-building Chandler campus (PHX1 through PHX8) totaling a publicly stated 169 MW of IT capacity across the whole campus; that campus-wide MW figure is not confirmed as this individual building's own capacity, so it is not asserted here as a single-building number.

Wikipedia's entry on CyrusOne states the company acquired 55.9 acres in Chandler in September 2011 for data center construction, part of its early-2010s national expansion under then-parent Cincinnati Bell before CyrusOne's own 2013 IPO; the company was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and was taken private in a roughly $15 billion deal when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it, closing in March 2022. Chandler's electric and water utility, Salt River Project (SRP), serves this part of the Phoenix metro; Arizona data centers' water-intensive cooling systems have drawn scrutiny from local outlets including the Phoenix New Times given the state's arid climate and ongoing water-supply debates, a regional context relevant to this campus though not a site-specific consumption figure confirmed for this particular building.

Chandler's broader appeal to data center operators, alongside CyrusOne, the same submarket has drawn large campuses from other hyperscale and colocation players, stems from Arizona's relatively low natural-disaster risk profile (limited seismic activity, no hurricane exposure), business-friendly tax treatment for data center equipment under state statute, and proximity to fiber routes linking Phoenix to Los Angeles and other West Coast interconnection points, factors industry trade press has repeatedly cited in explaining the Phoenix metro's growth as a secondary US data center hub behind Northern Virginia and Texas.

reading.body:
PHX6 is one building in CyrusOne's Chandler campus on South Ellis Street in Arizona, a multi-building complex with 169 MW of total IT capacity published for the entire site. The campus's published capacity makes it the fifth-largest facility by announced power in Arizona, where only four of 56 mapped data centers publish figures and the total announced capacity across the state is 512 MW. PHX6 itself occupies 2 million square feet, but the operator has not published an individual power rating for this building separate from the campus total.

Without a facility-specific power figure, the strategic weight of PHX6 cannot be read from published specifications alone. If the 169 MW campus capacity distributed evenly across eight buildings, PHX6 would represent roughly 21 MW of IT load, which at 40 kW per rack would suggest approximately 525 racks, an assumption offered only to indicate scale. The actual draw of this building remains unpublished and would determine whether it contributes meaningfully to Arizona's AI infrastructure.

Arizona's data center footprint is severely under-specified in public records, with 56 mapped sites but only 4 publishing capacity and 52 remaining dark to this registry. The Chandler campus is one of the few anchors with a public commitment to power, but the fragmentation of its capacity across eight buildings and the absence of individual building ratings limits what these specifications reveal about where compute density actually concentrates on this campus.
